parts.prompt: The region $$R$$ is the base of a solid. Cross sections perpendicular to the x-axis are squares. Find the volume of the solid.

rubric.criterion: Writes the integral of the side length squared.

parts.prompt: Find the area of the region enclosed by $$r = 2 + \cos\theta$$.
Find the area of the region inside $$r = 2 + \cos\theta$$ and outside $$r = 1.5$$.

rubric.criterion: Writes outer squared minus inner squared.

parts.prompt: Find $$\frac{dr}{d\theta}$$ at $$\theta = 2$$. Is the curve moving toward or away from the origin at that angle? Explain.

rubric.example: Since $$r > 0$$ and $$\frac{dr}{d\theta} < 0$$, the curve is moving toward the origin.

parts.prompt: Find the slope of the line tangent to $$r = 2 + \cos\theta$$ at $$\theta = 2$$.

questions.title: An accumulation function from a graph

rubric.criterion: Uses $$g'' = f'$$, the slope of the segment.

parts.prompt: On the open interval $$0 < x < 6$$, find all values of $$x$$ at which $$g$$ has a relative maximum. Justify your answer.

rubric.criterion: Identifies the correct values (or that there are none).
Justifies using a sign change of $$g' = f$$ from positive to negative.
rubric.example: $$g' = f$$ changes from positive to negative there.

parts.prompt: Find the absolute maximum value of $$g$$ on $$0 \leq x \leq 6$$. Justify your answer.

rubric.criterion: Considers the endpoints and every critical point (Candidates Test).

parts.prompt: Find the slope of the slope-field segment at each of the points $$(-1, 2)$$, $$(0, 3)$$, $$(1, 0)$$ and $$(2, 1)$$.
Write an equation for the line tangent to the graph of $$f$$ at $$x = 1$$, and use it to approximate $$f(1.2)$$.

rubric.criterion: Finds the slope at the point and writes the tangent line.

parts.prompt: Find $$\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}$$ in terms of $$x$$ and $$y$$. Is the approximation in part (b) an overestimate or an underestimate? Explain.

rubric.criterion: Uses the sign of the second derivative at the point to conclude.
rubric.example: At $$(1, -2)$$, $$\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = -18$$, so f is concave down and the tangent line lies above the curve: an overestimate.

parts.prompt: Find the particular solution $$y = f(x)$$ with $$f(1) = -2$$.
Show that $$\frac{dy}{dx} = -\frac{2x + y}{x + 2y}$$.

rubric.criterion: Differentiates implicitly, using the product rule on the $$xy$$ term.
Solves for $$\frac{dy}{dx}$$ to reach the given expression.

parts.prompt: Write an equation for the line tangent to the curve at the point $$(-1, -1)$$.

rubric.criterion: Finds the slope and writes the line.

parts.prompt: Find the coordinates of every point on the curve at which the tangent line is horizontal.

rubric.criterion: Sets the numerator equal to zero.
Substitutes into the curve and solves.

parts.prompt: Find $$\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}$$ at the point $$(-1, -1)$$.

rubric.criterion: Differentiates $$\frac{dy}{dx}$$ with the quotient rule, treating $$y$$ as a function of $$x$$.

parts.prompt: Find the interval of convergence of the series. Show the work that leads to your answer.

rubric.criterion: Analyzes both endpoints with a test.
rubric.example: At $$x = 3$$: $$\sum \frac{(-1)^{n+1}}{n}$$ converges (alternating series test). At $$x = -3$$: $$-\sum \frac{1}{n}$$ diverges (harmonic).

parts.prompt: Find the first three nonzero terms and the general term of the Maclaurin series for $$f'(x)$$. Then write $$f'(x)$$ as a rational function.
Use the first two nonzero terms of the series to approximate $$f(1)$$. Show that this approximation differs from $$f(1)$$ by less than $$0.019$$.

rubric.criterion: Uses the alternating series error bound with justification.
rubric.example: The series at $$x = 1$$ alternates with terms decreasing to 0, so the error is at most the third term, $$\frac{1}{3\cdot 27} = \frac{1}{81}$$.
